text:
harper: quick report from the onboarding lab: Node quickstart triggers 429s when users page embeddings rapidly.
liam: saw it. sample does naive parallel pagination and our tenant burst quota trips.
zoe: can you paste the snippet?
harper: ```js
// naive
await Promise.all(cursors.map(c => client.embeddings.page({ cursor: c })))
```
liam: that plus immediate retries = multiplier effect. retry has no jitter currently.
harper: two issues: (1) JS SDK doesn't export the internal limiter so sample authors can't opt into a shared token-bucket, (2) auth refresh race causes a thundering herd of 401->retry.
zoe: SDK parity gap — python has a public RateLimiter object. proposal: export a tiny `createRateLimiter({permitsPerSec, burst})` from JS root. mark it stable.
liam: short-term sample patch: use p-limit(3) and add a "Concurrency & 429" quickstart note. long-term: export limiter + paginator concurrency.
harper: auth fix: singleflight the refresh. implement `auth.singleflightRefresh()` that returns the inflight promise if present so only one refresh occurs.
zoe: also standardize retry backoff with jitter: `delay = Math.min(2000, base * 2**attempt) * (0.7 + Math.random()*0.6)`. spreads retries, bounds client-side pressure.
liam: small ergonomics idea: add `concurrency` param to paginator helper: `for await (const p of client.embeddings.paginate(q, { concurrency: 2 })) {}` keeps developer UX same but limits parallel requests.
harper: support wants header instrumentation: `x-client-concurrency` so they can correlate client-side concurrency in logs. low overhead.
ops-bot: created PR preview: https://deployments.redwood-inference.dev/pr/703 (includes p-limit sample + KB)
docs-bot: I'll add quickstart checkbox: "If you see 429s while paging: reduce concurrency, use the SDK RateLimiter, or enable jittered backoff" and link examples.
zoe: can we add a tiny benchmark script in devtools to show tokens/sec vs concurrency so users can tune? low effort, high signal.
liam: agreed. I'll ship sample patch + auth singleflight today, then follow up with SDK export & paginator concurrency early next week.
harper: thanks — this should cut onboarding tickets a lot. :slightly_smiling_face:
